_doc: Wikimedia Commons CANDIDATE manifest (research only — nothing here is downloaded or shown). Built by the imagery lane from WebSearch results restricted to commons.wikimedia.org, because this sandbox's network policy blocks the Wikimedia hosts. Every File: title is copied from a search result (or a Commons category listing a result showed); nothing is guessed. confidence 'high' = the file title (or its description, as the result showed it) names that exact place; 'med' = a description or category points to it but the title is generic or the photo may not show the place today; 'low' is never recorded. A candidate is a lead, not a verdict: tools/beta/imagery/fetch-commons.js re-reads every file from the Commons API on a GitHub runner (licence, author, description, categories, size) and refuses anything that is not a free licence or whose title/description/categories do not name the place. Targets without candidates that cite a Wikipedia article may be resolved from that article's lead image with --wiki-lead (same checks). Never: food places, venues, closed places, Vietnam. How-to: design/beta/IMAGERY.md § Commons.
licencePolicy: CC0, public domain, CC BY, CC BY-SA (any version, any port). NC and ND refused. GFDL-only refused. Credit (TASL) shown wherever the photo appears.

fields.type: hero = city/town/country hub scene (a slot, not a record); landmark = one tier-1 sight record
fields.names: phrases a file title, description or category must contain (compared without spaces, punctuation or diacritics) for the fetch to keep it
fields.priority: W8: 'lead' = the guide's lead card, 'row' = its first rail row (what a visitor sees first) — fetched right after the heroes
fields.wikiLead: W8: when no candidate passes, try the lead image of the record's cited Wikipedia article (same licence, depicts, subject and author checks) without --wiki-lead
fields.pilot: true for the pilot pages (Tokyo, Cleveland, New York, Chinatown SG, Wheeling) and the five live country hubs — fetched first
fields.skip: why this target never gets a photo (venue, modern public art, interior exhibit) or a stated gap
fields.candidates[].file: the Commons file title exactly as returned (File:…)
fields.candidates[].depicts: what the result says the photo shows
fields.candidates[].refused: set after a person looked at the fetched photo: why it is never used again (the fetch skips it)
fields.candidates[].flags: people-visible, public-art-check (no freedom of panorama for modern public art in the US/JP), venue-check, panorama (360° file), outdated (the place has changed), author-check — the fetch skips a flagged candidate unless --allow-flag names it
